headline: KSE-100 sheds 1,965 points as Islamabad imposes emergency in KP, while a deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport jolts Gulf markets and sends Brent above $106
mood: Risk-off on two fronts · Pakistan's political shock meets a Gulf security spike

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Sheds 1,965 Points as Islamabad Imposes KP Emergency
five_things.html: The KSE-100 fell 1,964.86 points (−1.18%) to close at 165,124.41 on Monday, reversing from an intraday high of 166,988.32 after President Asif Ali Zardari approved Governor's Rule/emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, with a joint sitting of parliament called for today to ratify the move following the collapse of government–PTI talks over counterterrorism policy. Breadth was lopsided at 85 decliners to 13 advancers (2 unchanged) on thinned volume of 104.27 million index shares (Rs14.5bn market-wide), with United Bank (−186.93 pts), Oil & Gas Development (−131.40), Habib Bank (−114.71) and Meezan Bank (−114.08) leading the rout — the 14-bank sub-index alone cost 734 points, 37% of the day's fall — while Colgate-Palmolive (+16.08) and Pakistan Tobacco bucked the trend. Pakera and The Nation confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Deadly Houthi Strike on Riyadh Airport Jolts Gulf Markets
five_things.html: A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the weekend killed more than a dozen people and injured over 300, prompting airlines to cancel flights and sending Gulf equities lower even as oil climbed: the Tadawul All-Share Index closed 0.2% lower at 10,361 (Saudi National Bank −1.1%, Aramco −0.2%) and Qatar's index fell 1.5% to its lowest since May 2020. Brent rose 1.8% to settle at $106.65 and WTI gained 2.0% to $93.74 as traders priced a fresh supply-risk premium on top of ongoing Bab al-Mandeb clashes. Business Recorder and CNBC confirm the moves.
five_things.sentiment: security shock outweighs the oil windfall

five_things.chip: Fed December Hike Odds Climb Near 88%, Pressuring Gold
five_things.html: Fed-funds futures now price roughly 88% odds of a December rate hike (versus just ~17% for the 28 October meeting), consistent with 16 of 19 FOMC members' dot-plot calls for at least one more 2026 move; the 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.24% and the 2-year near 4.80%. The repricing, alongside a firmer dollar and the oil-driven inflation scare, pulled gold down 0.59% to $4,168.90 and silver down 0.96% to $60.12. Kitco and CNBC confirm the pricing.

five_things.chip: Pakistan's $1.2bn IMF Tranche Awaits Board Nod as SBP Holds at 11.5%
five_things.html: Islamabad's $1.2 billion staff-level agreement with the IMF on the fourth EFF and third RSF reviews — reached 7–8 October — remains pending Executive Board approval, which would lift cumulative programme inflows to $5.7bn. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting on 14 September, September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y from 11.1% in August, and 3-month KIBOR sat near 11.5–11.75%, while USD/PKR held broadly steady at 276.97 interbank. Dawn and Trading Economics confirm the figures.
five_things.sentiment: genuine policy progress, overshadowed by politics

five_things.chip: US Stocks Mixed as Memory-Chip Slide Offsets Dow's Gain
five_things.html: Wall Street closed mixed Monday: the Dow added 0.38% to 51,850.55 while the S&P 500 slipped 0.06% to 7,807.24 and the Nasdaq fell 0.44% to 27,245.90 as memory-chip names sold off on valuation jitters and the oil spike revived inflation concerns; separately, OPEC+ held November output quotas steady on 4 October, keeping Saudi Arabia at 10.5mb/d and Russia at 9.9mb/d as the group manages a market caught between improving physical supply and persistent geopolitical risk. Yahoo Finance and CNBC confirm the details.

legislative.policy_html: Governor's Rule imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Articles 232/234 after President Zardari's nod on 11 October; a joint sitting of parliament is called for 13 October to ratify the move.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: the federal government and security apparatus gain direct administrative control to pursue counterterrorism operations, and defense-linked names could see a sentiment lift. Loses: banks and broader equities, which absorbed 37% of Monday's 1,965-point KSE-100 decline as investors price a higher political-risk premium ahead of today's parliamentary vote.

legislative.policy_html: UAE's VAT Executive Regulation amendments (Cabinet Decision No. 149, effective 1 October) revising input-tax apportionment, alongside OPEC+'s decision to hold November output quotas steady.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: large compliant UAE corporates and banks adapting to the new apportionment rules, and Gulf oil producers/energy equities benefiting from supply discipline plus a fresh geopolitical risk premium. Loses: SMEs facing heavier VAT-compliance costs, and broader Gulf equities (Tadawul −0.2%, Qatar −1.5% Monday) as the Riyadh airport attack adds a security discount that oil-price gains don't offset.

legislative.policy_html: The Fed's hawkish dot-plot (16 of 19 members projecting a further 2026 hike) now has futures pricing ~88% odds of a December hike, alongside the US continuing resolution funding the government through 11 December.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: near-term government-funding certainty for contractors and bond markets, and energy equities riding the Hormuz/Riyadh risk premium. Loses: growth and tech equities (Nasdaq −0.44% Monday) and precious metals (gold −0.59%, silver −0.96%) as a December hike firms up and yields stay elevated.

levels.resistance_note: Friday's close; then 168,580 if the KP crisis de-escalates

desk_stance_html: Monday's 1,965-point drop was a political-risk event, not a fundamentals one — the SBP's steady 11.5% rate, cooling CPI and the pending IMF tranche all argue for a floor, but today's parliamentary vote on the KP emergency is the near-term swing factor, and banks (37% of the fall) need to stabilise before we'd trust a bounce back above 167,089. Globally, the Riyadh airport attack and a firming ~88% probability of a December Fed hike are a reminder that geopolitical and rate risk can both bite at once, even as oil's rise is a mixed blessing for Gulf-linked flows into Pakistan. Our stance: trim leverage into the parliamentary vote, avoid chasing a dead-cat bounce in banks, and watch Brent/WTI and KP headlines as the swing factors for both the rupee and risk appetite. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 sheds 1,965 points as Islamabad imposes emergency in KP — while a deadly Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport jolts Gulf markets and sends Brent above $106.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US stocks closed mixed Monday as an oil-driven inflation scare and a slide in memory-chip names offset a rotation into value: the Dow added 0.38% to 51,850.55, while the S&P 500 eased 0.06% to 7,807.24 and the Nasdaq fell 0.44% to 27,245.90. Treasury yields held near multi-decade highs (10Y 5.24%, 2Y 4.80%) as Fed-funds futures now price roughly 88% odds of a December hike versus just ~17% for the 28 October meeting, consistent with 16 of 19 FOMC members' dot-plot calls for a further 2026 move. The same repricing pulled gold down 0.59% to $4,168.90 and silver down 0.96% to $60.12.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 1,964.86 points (-1.18%) to close at 165,124.41, reversing from an intraday high of 166,988.32 after President Asif Ali Zardari approved Governor's Rule/emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday, with a joint sitting of parliament called for today to ratify the move following the collapse of government-PTI talks over counterterrorism policy. Breadth was lopsided 85 decliners to 13 advancers on thinned volume (104.27m index shares, Rs14.5bn market-wide); United Bank, Oil & Gas Development, Habib Bank and Meezan Bank led the rout, with the 14-bank sub-index alone costing 734 points (37% of the fall). The selloff overshadowed real progress: the IMF's $1.2bn staff-level deal awaits Executive Board approval, the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5%, September CPI eased to 10.3% y/y, and the rupee held steady at 276.97 interbank.

GCC
A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport over the weekend killed more than a dozen people and injured over 300, grounding flights and sending the Tadawul All-Share Index down 0.2% to 10,361 while Qatar's index slid 1.5% to a post-May-2020 low. Brent settled up 1.8% at $106.65 and WTI up 2.0% at $93.74, and OPEC+ held November quotas steady on 4 October. Diversification momentum held firm regardless: Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI sat near a seven-month high of 55.3 in September and the UAE's matched that reading.

GLOBAL
Washington's funding fight stays parked under the continuing resolution through 11 December, though a narrower DHS funding lapse persists separately. The Fed's hawkish dot-plot keeps rate-sensitive equities and precious metals exposed as a December hike firms up.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: KP Governor's Rule heads to a parliamentary vote today — federal government/security apparatus wins administrative control; banks and equities absorb a political-risk discount.
• GCC: UAE VAT-rule overhaul + OPEC+ holding November output steady — compliant corporates and oil producers win; SMEs and broader Gulf equities lose ground after the Riyadh attack.
• Global: US funding certainty through 11 December vs. a ~88%-priced December Fed hike — contractors and bonds stabilise; tech equities and precious metals stay exposed.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 164,000 (deeper support 162,500), pivot 165,124 (Monday's close), resistance 167,089 then 168,580 if the KP crisis de-escalates. Our stance: trim leverage into the parliamentary vote, avoid chasing a dead-cat bounce in banks, and watch Brent/WTI and KP headlines as the swing factors for both the rupee and risk appetite. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
